text.text_excerpt: I had just left Forever New Orleans who had pointed me to Rouse's after I'd asked them where I could pick up something quick to eat without going through hustle n bustle of the French Quarter. So glad I'd asked! Love this convenient, friendly supermarket. I picked up some snacks, bottled water (it was $3 a bottle at the hotel!!), and also a sandwich from the deli. I did a quick walkthrough of all the aisle and like that they sold a lot of the local items at cheaper prices than I'd seen in the tourist shops. It seems small from the outside, but it's a pretty big space once you get inside. Will make a note to come here and stock up on snacks and drinks the next time I'm in NOLA and in this ...

Ahh downtown Rouses, please marry me and take me away from all the crappy Winn Dixies and Sav-a-Lots and Super Walmarts and all of those inferior supermarkets. They never appreciated me the way you do. Never. This Rouses lets me know it loves me by making sure I don't pass out from hunger while I drool at their yummy deli and cheese offerings. There are always samples. Good, yummy samples. Usually at least one aged gouda style cheese, gruyere or parm reg, pita chips and dips, and deli offerings. One Sunday morning, when this hungover mama needed it most, Rouses even sampled mimosas. It's like Rouses really knows me and loves me anyway. This Rouse's is a fantastic addition to the downtown area - the building is an old car dealership and is a great way to re-use the space. It's very central to a ton of people and also importantly close to the Superdome which means a lot of tailgaters can make use of Rouse's for their shopping or beverage needs. I do have to say that the prepared food usually looks average and not nearly as exciting as most upscale grocery stores but they do seem to draw a large lunch crowd so maybe there's something I'm missing. And the liquor is in a separate little customer service counter by the front door which keeps it safe from theft but makes it very difficult to see the prices listed on the shelve...
